Then the nobles of mankind would come and sit nearest to him, then the nobles of the jinn would come and sit next to mankind. Then he would call the birds, and they would shade them. Then he would call the wind, and it would carry them, and in a single morning it would travel the distance of a month.

Wahb, Ka'b and others said: When Sulayman, peace be upon him, became king after his father, he ordered that a throne be made for him to sit on for judging. He ordered that it be made in a wondrous and awe-inspiring form, so that whoever saw it, be he a wrongdoer or a false witness, would be deterred and awed. So he ordered that it be made of elephant tusks, inlaid with pearls, rubies and chrysolite, and that it be surrounded by golden palm trees. It was surrounded by four golden palm trees whose fronds were of red ruby and green emerald. On the top of two of the palm trees were golden peacocks, and on the top of two palm trees were golden eagles, facing one another. On either side of the throne they placed two golden lions, and on top of each of them was a pillar of green emerald.

They also wove over the palm trees vines of red gold, and made their clusters of red ruby, so that the canopy of the vines shaded the palm trees and the throne. When Sulayman, peace be upon him, wished to ascend it, he would place his feet on the lowest step, and the whole throne, with everything on it, would turn like a swiftly spinning millstone. The eagles and peacocks would spread their wings, the two lions would stretch out their forelegs, and they would strike the ground with their tails. This was done at every step that Sulayman climbed. When he reached the top, the two eagles that were on the palm trees would take Sulayman's crown and place it on his head. Then the throne would turn with everything on it, and the eagles, peacocks and two lions would turn with it, their heads inclined towards Sulayman, and they would sprinkle upon him musk and ambergris from their insides. Then a golden dove standing on a pillar of jewels above the throne would take up the Torah, and Sulayman, peace be upon him, would open it, read it to the people, and call them to decisive judgment.

They said: The leaders of the Children of Israel would sit on golden chairs inlaid with jewels, one thousand chairs to his right, and the leaders of the jinn would sit on silver chairs to his left, one thousand chairs. Then the birds would surround them and shade them, and the people would come forward for judgment. When the witnesses came forward to give their testimony, the throne would turn with everything on it and around him like a swiftly spinning millstone; the two lions would stretch out their forelegs and strike the ground with their tails, and the eagles and peacocks would spread their wings. The witnesses would be terrified, and they would testify only to the truth.

It was also said that what turned that throne was a golden serpent, upon which the throne rested, and it was greater than what Sakhr al-Jinni had made for him. When the eagles, lions and peacocks that were at the bottom of the throne sensed its turning, they would move up with it to the top. When they stopped, they would all stop at Sulayman's head while he was seated, and then they would all sprinkle upon his head what was in their insides of musk and ambergris.

When Sulayman died, Bakht Nasr sent someone who took the throne and carried it to Antioch. He wanted to ascend it, but he did not know how to climb it. When he placed his foot on it, the lion struck his leg and broke it, for Sulayman used to place both of his feet together when he climbed. Bakht Nasr died, and the throne was carried to Jerusalem. No king was ever able to sit on it. But no one knows the final outcome of its matter, and perhaps it was raised up (to heaven).

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Then he turned penitently﴾, meaning he returned to God and repented. This has already been discussed.

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿He said: "My Lord, forgive me"﴾, meaning forgive me my sin, "and grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me." It is asked: How could Sulayman seek worldly things when God has condemned them, hates them, and considers them insignificant? The answer is that the scholars interpret this as referring to the performance of God's rights, the governance of His kingdom, the ordering of the ranks of His creatures, the establishment of His limits, the preservation of His laws, the magnifying of His rituals, the manifestation of His worship, the necessity of obeying Him, and the ordering of the law of judgment that is enforced upon them by Him, and the fulfilment of the promise that He knows what none of His creatures knows, as He declared to His angels when He said: ﴿Indeed, I know what you do not know﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30]. Far be it from Sulayman, peace be upon him, that his request was a pursuit of the worldly life itself, for he and the prophets are the most detached of God's creatures from it. He only asked for its kingdom for God's sake, just as Nuh asked for its destruction and annihilation for God's sake. Both were praiseworthy and their requests were granted: Nuh's was answered and those upon the earth were destroyed, and Sulayman was given the kingdom. It has also been said that this was by a command from God, the Mighty and Majestic, in the manner that God knew only He could control, and no other of His servants could. Or he wished to say "a great kingdom," and then said: "that will not befit anyone after me." But this is questionable, and the first (view) is more correct.

Then He said to him: ﴿"This is Our gift, so give or withhold without account"﴾. Al-Hasan said: No one has been given a blessing by God except that he is held accountable for it, except Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon him, for He says: "This is Our gift" and so on. I say: This refutes what is reported in a khabar: "The last of the prophets to enter Paradise will be Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon him, because of his kingdom in this world." In some reports: "He will enter Paradise forty autumns after the prophets." This was mentioned by the author of al-Qut, and it is a hadith with no basis, because if His giving is without accountability, since it comes by way of grace, how could he be the last of the prophets to enter Paradise, when He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And indeed he has with Us a station of nearness and a good final return﴾? In the Sahih: "Every prophet has an answered supplication, and each prophet hastened his supplication," and the hadith continues. This has already been mentioned. So He made for him, before the request, a fulfilled need, and therefore there was no accountability for him. The meaning of his saying: "that will not befit anyone after me" is that no one should ask for it. It is as if he asked that no one else be allowed to ask after him, so that no one's hope would be attached to him, but he did not ask that the answer be withheld. It has also been said: His request for a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him was so that his place and honour with God would be manifest in the creation of the heavens and the earth. The prophets, peace be upon them, have a rivalry regarding their rank with Him, so each one loves to have a distinction by which his station with Him may be inferred. For this reason, when the Prophet (ﷺ) seized the 'ifrit who wanted to cut off his prayer, and God enabled him to overpower it, he wanted to tie it up, but then he remembered the words of his brother Sulayman: "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me," and so he sent it away humiliated. If anyone were given the like of it after him, the distinction would be gone, so he disliked that anyone should compete with him in that distinction, after he knew that it was a thing specific to him, the subjugation of the devils, and that he had been granted that no one would have it after him. And God knows best.

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running gently by his command wherever he wished﴾, meaning gentle despite its strength and power, so that it would not harm anyone, and it would carry him with his army, his troops and his procession. It is reported that his procession was a farsakh by a farsakh, a hundred levels one above another, each level a category of people, and he was at the highest level with his concubines, his attendants and his servants, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him.

Abu Nu'aym al-Hafiz mentioned: He narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Ja'far, who said: He narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, who said: He narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ayyub, who said: He narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash, from Idris ibn Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: My father narrated to me, saying: Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon him, had a thousand houses, the upper parts of which were of glass and the lower parts of iron. One day he rode the wind and passed by a ploughman, who looked at him and said: "The family of Dawud has been given a great kingdom!" The wind carried his words and cast them into Sulayman's ear. He said: So he descended until he came to the ploughman and said: "I heard your words, and I only came to you so that you would not wish for what you cannot have. A single glorification that God accepts from you is better than what the family of Dawud has been given." The ploughman said: "May God remove your worry as you have removed mine."

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿wherever he wished﴾, meaning wherever he intended. Mujahid said this. The Arabs say: "He hit the right thing and missed the answer" (aṣāba al-ṣawāb wa akhṭa'a al-jawāb), meaning he intended the right thing and missed the answer. Ibn al-A'rabi said this. A poet said:

*He hit upon the speech but could not...*
*and missed the answer at the joint.*

It is said that "aṣāba" means "intended" in the dialect of Himyar. Qatada said: it is in the language of Hajar. It is also said: "wherever he hit" means "whenever he aimed," derived from an arrow striking its intended target.

﴿And the devils, every builder and diver﴾, meaning We subjected to him the devils, and none had been subjected to anyone before him. "Every builder" is in apposition to "the devils," meaning every builder among them, so they would build for him whatever he wished. A poet said: [[This is al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani. Another version reads: "when the King said to him" and "then restrain them from the Fund." "Al-Fund" means error. "Khayyis" means subdue. "Al-Sifah" is the plural of "sifāḥa," which are thin, broad stones.]]

*Except Sulayman, when the God said to him:*
*"Stand among the wilderness and restrain them from error;*
*subdue the jinn, for I have permitted them*
*to build Tudmur with stone-slabs and pillars."*

"And diver" means in the sea, to bring up pearls for him. Sulayman was the first to have pearls extracted for him from the sea.

﴿And others bound together in shackles﴾, meaning We subjected to him the rebellious devils until he bound them in chains and iron fetters. Qatada said this. Al-Suddi said: "chains." Ibn 'Abbas said: "bonds." From this is the poet's saying [[This is 'Amr ibn Kulthum, and the verse is from his Mu'allaqa.]]:

*They returned with plunder and captives,*
*and we returned with kings in chains.*

Yahya ibn Sallam said: He would do this only to their disbelievers. When they believed, he would release them and not subject them.

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿"This is Our gift"﴾. The reference of "this" is to the kingdom: this kingdom is Our gift, so give to whomever you wish or withhold from whomever you wish, and there is no accountability for you. This is related from al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and others. Al-Hasan said: God has not bestowed a blessing on anyone except that he is held accountable for it, except Sulayman, peace be upon him, for God, the Exalted, says: "This is Our gift, so give or withhold without account." Qatada said: The reference in His saying "This is Our gift" is to what He gave him of power over intercourse. He had three hundred wives and seven hundred concubines, and in his loins was the semen of a hundred men. Ikrimah narrated this from Ibn 'Abbas [[Abu Hayyan said in his tafsir: "Perhaps this is not authentic from Ibn 'Abbas, because no mention of women has occurred here, nor of what he was given of power in that regard."]]. Its meaning is in al-Bukhari. And on this basis…

"Fa-mnun" (﻿فَامْنُنْ) is from al-mann (المَنّ), meaning the act of bestowing. It is said: amná yumnī and mana yamnī are two dialects; when you command one who uses amná, you say amni. It is also said: from mana yamnī fī al-amr, the command is imni; when you bring the nūn of the verb, the light nūn, you say "imnun." Whoever takes it to mean al-minna (favour) says: "manna ʿalayh" (he bestowed a favour upon him). When he puts it in the form of a command, he makes the two nūns manifest, because it is doubled, so he says "amnun" (﻿امْنُنْ).

It is related in the report that He subjected the devils to him, so whoever he wished he would bestow favour upon by freeing and releasing, and whoever he wished he would hold back. This is the view of Qatadah and al-Suddi. And according to what ʿIkrimah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: "Have intercourse with whichever of your wives you wish, and leave off intercourse with whichever of them you wish, with no reckoning against you."

"And indeed for him with Us is nearness and a good return" (﻿وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنا لَزُلْفى وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ): that is, if We bestow Our favour upon him in this world, then for him with Us in the Hereafter there is nearness (qurbah) and a good place of return (husn marji').

The commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 38, verses 34–40 (part 1 of 3):

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We certainly tried Solomon﴾. It was said: Solomon was tested after he had ruled for twenty years, and he ruled for twenty years after the trial. This was mentioned by al-Zamakhshari. "Fatannā" (we tried) means "ibtalaynā" (We tested) and "ʿāqabnā" (We punished). The cause of this is what Saʿid ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Two groups came to Solomon, peace be upon him, for judgment. One of them was from the people of Jarada, the wife of Solomon, whom he loved. He wished that the judgment would go in their favour. Then he judged between them with the truth, and what befell him was a punishment for that inclination.

Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib said: Solomon, peace be upon him, secluded himself from the people for three days, not judging between anyone and not granting justice to the wronged against the wrongdoer. So Allah the Exalted revealed to him: "I did not appoint you as a successor so that you would seclude yourself from My servants, but so that you would judge between them and grant justice to their wronged ones."

Shahr ibn Hawshab and Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Solomon, peace be upon him, captured the daughter of a king who had fought against him by sea, on an island among the islands of the sea called Sidon. Love for her was cast upon him, while she turned away from him. She would not look at him except sidelong, and would not speak to him except curtly. Her tears would not dry from grief for her father, and she was at the peak of beauty. Then she asked him to make for her a statue in the likeness of her father so that she could look at it. He ordered it made for her, and she revered it and prostrated to it, and her maidservants prostrated with her. It became an idol worshipped in his house while he did not know. Forty nights passed, and the news spread among the Children of Israel. Solomon learned of it, broke it, burned it, and then scattered it into the sea.

It was also said: When Solomon took the daughter of the king of Sidon, whose name was Jarada, according to what al-Zamakhshari mentioned, he admired her. He invited her to Islam, but she refused. He threatened her, and she said: "Kill me, but I will not become a Muslim." So he married her while she was a polytheist, and she used to worship an idol of hers made of ruby for forty days secretly from Solomon, until she became a Muslim. Solomon was punished by the loss of his kingdom for forty days.

Kaʿb al-Ahbar said: When he wronged the horses by killing them, his kingdom was taken from him.

al-Hasan said: He approached some of his wives during menstruation or something else.

It was also said: He was commanded not to marry any woman except from the Children of Israel, but he married a woman from outside them, and he was punished for that. And Allah knows best.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body﴾. It was said: It was a devil, according to the statement of most of the people of tafsir (exegesis). Allah cast upon it the likeness of Solomon, peace be upon him. His name was Sakhr ibn ʿUmayr, the Master of the Sea, and he is the one who guided Solomon to the diamond when Solomon ordered the building of Bayt al-Maqdis (the Holy House in Jerusalem). The stones would produce a sound when they were cut with iron, so they took diamonds and began to cut the stones, the gems, and other things with them, and they made no sound.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: He was a rebellious jinn whom all the devils could not overpower. He kept scheming until he obtained the ring of Solomon son of Dawud. Solomon would not enter the privy with his ring. So Sakhr came in the form of Solomon and took the ring from one of Solomon's women, a mother of a child of his called al-Amina, as Shahr and Wahb said. Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Jubayr said: Her name was Jarada. So he stood for forty days in Solomon's kingdom while Solomon was fleeing, until Allah restored the ring and the kingdom to him.

Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib said: Solomon had placed his ring under his bed, and the devil took it from under him.

Mujahid said: The devil took it from Solomon's hand, because Solomon asked the devil, whose name was Asif: "How do you lead people astray?" The devil said to him: "Give me your ring and I will tell you." So he gave him his ring. When the devil took the ring, he sat on Solomon's throne, taking his form, entering upon his wives, judging by other than the truth, and commanding other than what is right. [[These statements are certainly not authentic, because they contradict infallibility (ʿiṣmah), which is among the most distinctive attributes of the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them. Even if any of them were authentic, revelation would become subject to doubt and suspicion. Abu Hayyan said in his tafsir: "The exegetes have transmitted in this trial and the casting of the body statements that require the prophets to be absolved of them. They can be found in their books, and it is not permissible to transmit them. They are either fabrications of the Jews or the heretics. Allah did not specify what the trial was, nor the body that He cast upon Solomon's throne." He continued: "Someone whom the exegetes attribute to the one who is to be followed (i.e., Solomon) would not have said what is too grave to utter, and some of what they mentioned is impossible by reason, such as the devil taking the form of a prophet so that his affair becomes confused for the people, and they believe that the one they see is the prophet. Were this possible, one could not trust the sending of any prophet. This is merely a saying borrowed from the Sophists, the heretics. We ask Allah for the soundness of our minds and intellects from it." al-Alusi said: "Among the worst things in it is the claim that the devil gained power over the wives of his prophet to the point that he had intercourse with them while they were menstruating. Allahu Akbar!! This is a great slander and a grave matter." The author will also later weaken this statement.]]. There was a disagreement about his having intercourse with Solomon's wives. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas and Wahb ibn Munabbih that he used to approach them during their menstruation. Mujahid said: He was prevented from approaching them, and Solomon's kingdom was taken from him, so he fled to the seashore, begging from people and carrying the fish of the fishermen for a wage. Whenever he told people that he was Solomon, they called him a liar.

Qatada said: After the Children of Israel had disapproved of the judgment of the devil, Solomon took back his fish from a fisherman. It was said: He asked it as food. Ibn ʿAbbas said: He took it as a fee for carrying a fish. It was also said: Solomon caught it, and when he split its belly he found his ring inside it. This was forty days after the loss of his kingdom, which corresponds to the number of days during which the idol was worshipped in his house. He found the ring in the belly of the fish because the devil who had taken it had thrown it into the sea.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: While Solomon was on the seashore playing with his ring, it fell from him into the sea, and his kingdom was in his ring.

Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The engraving on the ring of Solomon son of Dawud was: There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

Yahya ibn Abi ʿAmr al-Shaybani related that Solomon found his ring in ʿAsqalan, and walked from there to Bayt al-Maqdis, humbling himself before Allah the Exalted.

Ibn ʿAbbas and others said: Then, when Allah restored his kingdom to Solomon, he seized Sakhr, who had taken his ring. He carved out a rock for him, put him inside it, sealed him in with another rock, fastened it with iron and lead, sealed it with his ring, and threw it into the sea, saying: "This is your prison until the Day of Resurrection."

ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, said: When Solomon took the ring, the devils, the jinn, the humans, the birds, the beasts, and the wind came to him. The devil who had been left in charge of his household fled and came to an island in the sea. They sent devils to him, and they said: "We cannot overpower him, but he comes to a spring on the island one day every seven days, and we cannot overpower him until he becomes intoxicated!" He said: So Solomon drained its water and put wine into it. When the day of its coming came, he found the wine and said: "By Allah, you are a good drink, except that you make the forbearing one act foolishly, and you increase the ignorant one in ignorance." Then he became extremely thirsty, and came to it again and said the same thing, and drank it. It overcame his mind, and they showed him the ring, and he said: "Hearing and obedience." They brought him to Solomon, who bound him and sent him to a mountain. They mentioned that it was the Mountain of Smoke, and said: "The smoke you see is from his breath, and the water that comes out of the mountain is from his urine."

Mujahid said: The name of that devil is Asif. Al-Suddi said: His name is Haqbiq. And Allah knows best. This statement has been weakened on the ground that the devil cannot take the form of the prophets, and also that it is impossible for the people of Solomon's kingdom to be confused about the devil being Solomon, so that they would think they were with their prophet in the truth, while they were with the devil in falsehood.

It was also said: The body was a child born to Solomon. When he was born, the devils gathered, and some of them said to others: "If a son survives to him, we will not be released from the trial and servitude we are in. So come, let us kill his son or maim him." Solomon learned of this, so he ordered the wind to carry the child up to the clouds, and his son grew up in the clouds, fearing the harm of the devils. Allah punished him through his fear of the devils, so he was not aware until he had fallen dead upon his throne. Al-Shaʿbi said this in meaning. This is the body of which Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body﴾.

al-Naqqash and others related: Solomon had most of his maidservants intercourse in pursuit of a child, so he had a child born to him who was half a human. This was the body placed upon his throne, which the midwife brought and then placed there.

In the Sahih of al-Bukhari and Muslim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Solomon said: Tonight I will go in to ninety women, and each of them will bear a horseman who will fight in the cause of Allah." His companion said to him: "Say: If Allah wills." But he did not say: "If Allah wills." So he went in to all of them, and only one woman became pregnant, and she brought forth half a man. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if he had said: "If Allah wills," they would have fought in the cause of Allah as horsemen, all of them."

It was also said: The body was Asif ibn Barkhiya, the truthful one, the scribe of Solomon. This is because when Solomon was tried, the ring fell from his hand, and his kingdom was in it. He put it back on his hand, and it fell again, and he became certain of the trial. Asif said to him: "You are being tested, and that is why it does not remain on your hand. So flee to Allah the Exalted, repenting of this. I will take your place in your world until Allah accepts your repentance. You have fourteen days from the time you were tried." So Solomon fled in haste to his Lord, and Asif took the ring and placed it on his hand, and it remained there. He had knowledge of the Book. Asif stood in Solomon's kingdom and his household, walking in his way and acting by his deeds, until Solomon returned to his home, repentant to Allah the Exalted, and Allah restored his kingdom to him. Then Asif remained in his place, sat on his throne, and took the ring.

It was also said: The body was Solomon himself, for he fell so severely ill that he became a body. The severely ill person is described by it, and it is said: "Like the cast-down body."

The description of Solomon's throne and his kingdom.

It is said on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: Sulayman would have six hundred thrones set out for him. Then the nobles of mankind would come and sit nearest to him, then the nobles of the jinn would come and sit next to mankind. Then he would call the birds, and they would shade them. Then he would call the wind, and it would carry them, and in a single morning it would travel the distance of a month.

Wahb, Ka'b and others said: When Sulayman, peace be upon him, became king after his father, he ordered that a throne be made for him to sit on for judging. He ordered that it be made in a wondrous and awe-inspiring form, so that whoever saw it, be he a wrongdoer or a false witness, would be deterred and awed. So he ordered that it be made of elephant tusks, inlaid with pearls, rubies and chrysolite, and that it be surrounded by golden palm trees. It was surrounded by four golden palm trees whose fronds were of red ruby and green emerald. On the top of two of the palm trees were golden peacocks, and on the top of two palm trees were golden eagles, facing one another. On either side of the throne they placed two golden lions, and on top of each of them was a pillar of green emerald.

They also wove over the palm trees vines of red gold, and made their clusters of red ruby, so that the canopy of the vines shaded the palm trees and the throne. When Sulayman, peace be upon him, wished to ascend it, he would place his feet on the lowest step, and the whole throne, with everything on it, would turn like a swiftly spinning millstone. The eagles and peacocks would spread their wings, the two lions would stretch out their forelegs, and they would strike the ground with their tails. This was done at every step that Sulayman climbed. When he reached the top, the two eagles that were on the palm trees would take Sulayman's crown and place it on his head. Then the throne would turn with everything on it, and the eagles, peacocks and two lions would turn with it, their heads inclined towards Sulayman, and they would sprinkle upon him musk and ambergris from their insides. Then a golden dove standing on a pillar of jewels above the throne would take up the Torah, and Sulayman, peace be upon him, would open it, read it to the people, and call them to decisive judgment.

They said: The leaders of the Children of Israel would sit on golden chairs inlaid with jewels, one thousand chairs to his right, and the leaders of the jinn would sit on silver chairs to his left, one thousand chairs. Then the birds would surround them and shade them, and the people would come forward for judgment. When the witnesses came forward to give their testimony, the throne would turn with everything on it and around him like a swiftly spinning millstone; the two lions would stretch out their forelegs and strike the ground with their tails, and the eagles and peacocks would spread their wings. The witnesses would be terrified, and they would testify only to the truth.

It was also said that what turned that throne was a golden serpent, upon which the throne rested, and it was greater than what Sakhr al-Jinni had made for him. When the eagles, lions and peacocks that were at the bottom of the throne sensed its turning, they would move up with it to the top. When they stopped, they would all stop at Sulayman's head while he was seated, and then they would all sprinkle upon his head what was in their insides of musk and ambergris.

When Sulayman died, Bakht Nasr sent someone who took the throne and carried it to Antioch. He wanted to ascend it, but he did not know how to climb it. When he placed his foot on it, the lion struck his leg and broke it, for Sulayman used to place both of his feet together when he climbed. Bakht Nasr died, and the throne was carried to Jerusalem. No king was ever able to sit on it. But no one knows the final outcome of its matter, and perhaps it was raised up (to heaven).

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Then he turned penitently﴾, meaning he returned to God and repented. This has already been discussed.

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿He said: "My Lord, forgive me"﴾, meaning forgive me my sin, "and grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me." It is asked: How could Sulayman seek worldly things when God has condemned them, hates them, and considers them insignificant? The answer is that the scholars interpret this as referring to the performance of God's rights, the governance of His kingdom, the ordering of the ranks of His creatures, the establishment of His limits, the preservation of His laws, the magnifying of His rituals, the manifestation of His worship, the necessity of obeying Him, and the ordering of the law of judgment that is enforced upon them by Him, and the fulfilment of the promise that He knows what none of His creatures knows, as He declared to His angels when He said: ﴿Indeed, I know what you do not know﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30]. Far be it from Sulayman, peace be upon him, that his request was a pursuit of the worldly life itself, for he and the prophets are the most detached of God's creatures from it. He only asked for its kingdom for God's sake, just as Nuh asked for its destruction and annihilation for God's sake. Both were praiseworthy and their requests were granted: Nuh's was answered and those upon the earth were destroyed, and Sulayman was given the kingdom. It has also been said that this was by a command from God, the Mighty and Majestic, in the manner that God knew only He could control, and no other of His servants could. Or he wished to say "a great kingdom," and then said: "that will not befit anyone after me." But this is questionable, and the first (view) is more correct.

Then He said to him: ﴿"This is Our gift, so give or withhold without account"﴾. Al-Hasan said: No one has been given a blessing by God except that he is held accountable for it, except Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon him, for He says: "This is Our gift" and so on. I say: This refutes what is reported in a khabar: "The last of the prophets to enter Paradise will be Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon him, because of his kingdom in this world." In some reports: "He will enter Paradise forty autumns after the prophets." This was mentioned by the author of al-Qut, and it is a hadith with no basis, because if His giving is without accountability, since it comes by way of grace, how could he be the last of the prophets to enter Paradise, when He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And indeed he has with Us a station of nearness and a good final return﴾? In the Sahih: "Every prophet has an answered supplication, and each prophet hastened his supplication," and the hadith continues. This has already been mentioned. So He made for him, before the request, a fulfilled need, and therefore there was no accountability for him. The meaning of his saying: "that will not befit anyone after me" is that no one should ask for it. It is as if he asked that no one else be allowed to ask after him, so that no one's hope would be attached to him, but he did not ask that the answer be withheld. It has also been said: His request for a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him was so that his place and honour with God would be manifest in the creation of the heavens and the earth. The prophets, peace be upon them, have a rivalry regarding their rank with Him, so each one loves to have a distinction by which his station with Him may be inferred. For this reason, when the Prophet (ﷺ) seized the 'ifrit who wanted to cut off his prayer, and God enabled him to overpower it, he wanted to tie it up, but then he remembered the words of his brother Sulayman: "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me," and so he sent it away humiliated. If anyone were given the like of it after him, the distinction would be gone, so he disliked that anyone should compete with him in that distinction, after he knew that it was a thing specific to him, the subjugation of the devils, and that he had been granted that no one would have it after him. And God knows best.

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running gently by his command wherever he wished﴾, meaning gentle despite its strength and power, so that it would not harm anyone, and it would carry him with his army, his troops and his procession. It is reported that his procession was a farsakh by a farsakh, a hundred levels one above another, each level a category of people, and he was at the highest level with his concubines, his attendants and his servants, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him.

Abu Nu'aym al-Hafiz mentioned: He narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Ja'far, who said: He narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, who said: He narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ayyub, who said: He narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash, from Idris ibn Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: My father narrated to me, saying: Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon him, had a thousand houses, the upper parts of which were of glass and the lower parts of iron. One day he rode the wind and passed by a ploughman, who looked at him and said: "The family of Dawud has been given a great kingdom!" The wind carried his words and cast them into Sulayman's ear. He said: So he descended until he came to the ploughman and said: "I heard your words, and I only came to you so that you would not wish for what you cannot have. A single glorification that God accepts from you is better than what the family of Dawud has been given." The ploughman said: "May God remove your worry as you have removed mine."

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿wherever he wished﴾, meaning wherever he intended. Mujahid said this. The Arabs say: "He hit the right thing and missed the answer" (aṣāba al-ṣawāb wa akhṭa'a al-jawāb), meaning he intended the right thing and missed the answer. Ibn al-A'rabi said this. A poet said:

*He hit upon the speech but could not...*
*and missed the answer at the joint.*

It is said that "aṣāba" means "intended" in the dialect of Himyar. Qatada said: it is in the language of Hajar. It is also said: "wherever he hit" means "whenever he aimed," derived from an arrow striking its intended target.

﴿And the devils, every builder and diver﴾, meaning We subjected to him the devils, and none had been subjected to anyone before him. "Every builder" is in apposition to "the devils," meaning every builder among them, so they would build for him whatever he wished. A poet said: [[This is al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani. Another version reads: "when the King said to him" and "then restrain them from the Fund." "Al-Fund" means error. "Khayyis" means subdue. "Al-Sifah" is the plural of "sifāḥa," which are thin, broad stones.]]

*Except Sulayman, when the God said to him:*
*"Stand among the wilderness and restrain them from error;*
*subdue the jinn, for I have permitted them*
*to build Tudmur with stone-slabs and pillars."*

"And diver" means in the sea, to bring up pearls for him. Sulayman was the first to have pearls extracted for him from the sea.

﴿And others bound together in shackles﴾, meaning We subjected to him the rebellious devils until he bound them in chains and iron fetters. Qatada said this. Al-Suddi said: "chains." Ibn 'Abbas said: "bonds." From this is the poet's saying [[This is 'Amr ibn Kulthum, and the verse is from his Mu'allaqa.]]:

*They returned with plunder and captives,*
*and we returned with kings in chains.*

Yahya ibn Sallam said: He would do this only to their disbelievers. When they believed, he would release them and not subject them.

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿"This is Our gift"﴾. The reference of "this" is to the kingdom: this kingdom is Our gift, so give to whomever you wish or withhold from whomever you wish, and there is no accountability for you. This is related from al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and others. Al-Hasan said: God has not bestowed a blessing on anyone except that he is held accountable for it, except Sulayman, peace be upon him, for God, the Exalted, says: "This is Our gift, so give or withhold without account." Qatada said: The reference in His saying "This is Our gift" is to what He gave him of power over intercourse. He had three hundred wives and seven hundred concubines, and in his loins was the semen of a hundred men. Ikrimah narrated this from Ibn 'Abbas [[Abu Hayyan said in his tafsir: "Perhaps this is not authentic from Ibn 'Abbas, because no mention of women has occurred here, nor of what he was given of power in that regard."]]. Its meaning is in al-Bukhari. And on this basis…

"Fa-mnun" (﻿فَامْنُنْ) is from al-mann (المَنّ), meaning the act of bestowing. It is said: amná yumnī and mana yamnī are two dialects; when you command one who uses amná, you say amni. It is also said: from mana yamnī fī al-amr, the command is imni; when you bring the nūn of the verb, the light nūn, you say "imnun." Whoever takes it to mean al-minna (favour) says: "manna ʿalayh" (he bestowed a favour upon him). When he puts it in the form of a command, he makes the two nūns manifest, because it is doubled, so he says "amnun" (﻿امْنُنْ).

It is related in the report that He subjected the devils to him, so whoever he wished he would bestow favour upon by freeing and releasing, and whoever he wished he would hold back. This is the view of Qatadah and al-Suddi. And according to what ʿIkrimah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: "Have intercourse with whichever of your wives you wish, and leave off intercourse with whichever of them you wish, with no reckoning against you."

"And indeed for him with Us is nearness and a good return" (﻿وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنا لَزُلْفى وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ): that is, if We bestow Our favour upon him in this world, then for him with Us in the Hereafter there is nearness (qurbah) and a good place of return (husn marji').

The commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 38, verses 34–40 (part 1 of 3):

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We certainly tried Solomon﴾. It was said: Solomon was tested after he had ruled for twenty years, and he ruled for twenty years after the trial. This was mentioned by al-Zamakhshari. "Fatannā" (we tried) means "ibtalaynā" (We tested) and "ʿāqabnā" (We punished). The cause of this is what Saʿid ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Two groups came to Solomon, peace be upon him, for judgment. One of them was from the people of Jarada, the wife of Solomon, whom he loved. He wished that the judgment would go in their favour. Then he judged between them with the truth, and what befell him was a punishment for that inclination.

Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib said: Solomon, peace be upon him, secluded himself from the people for three days, not judging between anyone and not granting justice to the wronged against the wrongdoer. So Allah the Exalted revealed to him: "I did not appoint you as a successor so that you would seclude yourself from My servants, but so that you would judge between them and grant justice to their wronged ones."

Shahr ibn Hawshab and Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Solomon, peace be upon him, captured the daughter of a king who had fought against him by sea, on an island among the islands of the sea called Sidon. Love for her was cast upon him, while she turned away from him. She would not look at him except sidelong, and would not speak to him except curtly. Her tears would not dry from grief for her father, and she was at the peak of beauty. Then she asked him to make for her a statue in the likeness of her father so that she could look at it. He ordered it made for her, and she revered it and prostrated to it, and her maidservants prostrated with her. It became an idol worshipped in his house while he did not know. Forty nights passed, and the news spread among the Children of Israel. Solomon learned of it, broke it, burned it, and then scattered it into the sea.

It was also said: When Solomon took the daughter of the king of Sidon, whose name was Jarada, according to what al-Zamakhshari mentioned, he admired her. He invited her to Islam, but she refused. He threatened her, and she said: "Kill me, but I will not become a Muslim." So he married her while she was a polytheist, and she used to worship an idol of hers made of ruby for forty days secretly from Solomon, until she became a Muslim. Solomon was punished by the loss of his kingdom for forty days.

Kaʿb al-Ahbar said: When he wronged the horses by killing them, his kingdom was taken from him.

al-Hasan said: He approached some of his wives during menstruation or something else.

It was also said: He was commanded not to marry any woman except from the Children of Israel, but he married a woman from outside them, and he was punished for that. And Allah knows best.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body﴾. It was said: It was a devil, according to the statement of most of the people of tafsir (exegesis). Allah cast upon it the likeness of Solomon, peace be upon him. His name was Sakhr ibn ʿUmayr, the Master of the Sea, and he is the one who guided Solomon to the diamond when Solomon ordered the building of Bayt al-Maqdis (the Holy House in Jerusalem). The stones would produce a sound when they were cut with iron, so they took diamonds and began to cut the stones, the gems, and other things with them, and they made no sound.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: He was a rebellious jinn whom all the devils could not overpower. He kept scheming until he obtained the ring of Solomon son of Dawud. Solomon would not enter the privy with his ring. So Sakhr came in the form of Solomon and took the ring from one of Solomon's women, a mother of a child of his called al-Amina, as Shahr and Wahb said. Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Jubayr said: Her name was Jarada. So he stood for forty days in Solomon's kingdom while Solomon was fleeing, until Allah restored the ring and the kingdom to him.

Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib said: Solomon had placed his ring under his bed, and the devil took it from under him.

Mujahid said: The devil took it from Solomon's hand, because Solomon asked the devil, whose name was Asif: "How do you lead people astray?" The devil said to him: "Give me your ring and I will tell you." So he gave him his ring. When the devil took the ring, he sat on Solomon's throne, taking his form, entering upon his wives, judging by other than the truth, and commanding other than what is right. [[These statements are certainly not authentic, because they contradict infallibility (ʿiṣmah), which is among the most distinctive attributes of the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them. Even if any of them were authentic, revelation would become subject to doubt and suspicion. Abu Hayyan said in his tafsir: "The exegetes have transmitted in this trial and the casting of the body statements that require the prophets to be absolved of them. They can be found in their books, and it is not permissible to transmit them. They are either fabrications of the Jews or the heretics. Allah did not specify what the trial was, nor the body that He cast upon Solomon's throne." He continued: "Someone whom the exegetes attribute to the one who is to be followed (i.e., Solomon) would not have said what is too grave to utter, and some of what they mentioned is impossible by reason, such as the devil taking the form of a prophet so that his affair becomes confused for the people, and they believe that the one they see is the prophet. Were this possible, one could not trust the sending of any prophet. This is merely a saying borrowed from the Sophists, the heretics. We ask Allah for the soundness of our minds and intellects from it." al-Alusi said: "Among the worst things in it is the claim that the devil gained power over the wives of his prophet to the point that he had intercourse with them while they were menstruating. Allahu Akbar!! This is a great slander and a grave matter." The author will also later weaken this statement.]]. There was a disagreement about his having intercourse with Solomon's wives. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas and Wahb ibn Munabbih that he used to approach them during their menstruation. Mujahid said: He was prevented from approaching them, and Solomon's kingdom was taken from him, so he fled to the seashore, begging from people and carrying the fish of the fishermen for a wage. Whenever he told people that he was Solomon, they called him a liar.

Qatada said: After the Children of Israel had disapproved of the judgment of the devil, Solomon took back his fish from a fisherman. It was said: He asked it as food. Ibn ʿAbbas said: He took it as a fee for carrying a fish. It was also said: Solomon caught it, and when he split its belly he found his ring inside it. This was forty days after the loss of his kingdom, which corresponds to the number of days during which the idol was worshipped in his house. He found the ring in the belly of the fish because the devil who had taken it had thrown it into the sea.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: While Solomon was on the seashore playing with his ring, it fell from him into the sea, and his kingdom was in his ring.

Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The engraving on the ring of Solomon son of Dawud was: There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

Yahya ibn Abi ʿAmr al-Shaybani related that Solomon found his ring in ʿAsqalan, and walked from there to Bayt al-Maqdis, humbling himself before Allah the Exalted.

Ibn ʿAbbas and others said: Then, when Allah restored his kingdom to Solomon, he seized Sakhr, who had taken his ring. He carved out a rock for him, put him inside it, sealed him in with another rock, fastened it with iron and lead, sealed it with his ring, and threw it into the sea, saying: "This is your prison until the Day of Resurrection."

ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, said: When Solomon took the ring, the devils, the jinn, the humans, the birds, the beasts, and the wind came to him. The devil who had been left in charge of his household fled and came to an island in the sea. They sent devils to him, and they said: "We cannot overpower him, but he comes to a spring on the island one day every seven days, and we cannot overpower him until he becomes intoxicated!" He said: So Solomon drained its water and put wine into it. When the day of its coming came, he found the wine and said: "By Allah, you are a good drink, except that you make the forbearing one act foolishly, and you increase the ignorant one in ignorance." Then he became extremely thirsty, and came to it again and said the same thing, and drank it. It overcame his mind, and they showed him the ring, and he said: "Hearing and obedience." They brought him to Solomon, who bound him and sent him to a mountain. They mentioned that it was the Mountain of Smoke, and said: "The smoke you see is from his breath, and the water that comes out of the mountain is from his urine."

Mujahid said: The name of that devil is Asif. Al-Suddi said: His name is Haqbiq. And Allah knows best. This statement has been weakened on the ground that the devil cannot take the form of the prophets, and also that it is impossible for the people of Solomon's kingdom to be confused about the devil being Solomon, so that they would think they were with their prophet in the truth, while they were with the devil in falsehood.

It was also said: The body was a child born to Solomon. When he was born, the devils gathered, and some of them said to others: "If a son survives to him, we will not be released from the trial and servitude we are in. So come, let us kill his son or maim him." Solomon learned of this, so he ordered the wind to carry the child up to the clouds, and his son grew up in the clouds, fearing the harm of the devils. Allah punished him through his fear of the devils, so he was not aware until he had fallen dead upon his throne. Al-Shaʿbi said this in meaning. This is the body of which Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body﴾.

al-Naqqash and others related: Solomon had most of his maidservants intercourse in pursuit of a child, so he had a child born to him who was half a human. This was the body placed upon his throne, which the midwife brought and then placed there.

In the Sahih of al-Bukhari and Muslim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Solomon said: Tonight I will go in to ninety women, and each of them will bear a horseman who will fight in the cause of Allah." His companion said to him: "Say: If Allah wills." But he did not say: "If Allah wills." So he went in to all of them, and only one woman became pregnant, and she brought forth half a man. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if he had said: "If Allah wills," they would have fought in the cause of Allah as horsemen, all of them."

It was also said: The body was Asif ibn Barkhiya, the truthful one, the scribe of Solomon. This is because when Solomon was tried, the ring fell from his hand, and his kingdom was in it. He put it back on his hand, and it fell again, and he became certain of the trial. Asif said to him: "You are being tested, and that is why it does not remain on your hand. So flee to Allah the Exalted, repenting of this. I will take your place in your world until Allah accepts your repentance. You have fourteen days from the time you were tried." So Solomon fled in haste to his Lord, and Asif took the ring and placed it on his hand, and it remained there. He had knowledge of the Book. Asif stood in Solomon's kingdom and his household, walking in his way and acting by his deeds, until Solomon returned to his home, repentant to Allah the Exalted, and Allah restored his kingdom to him. Then Asif remained in his place, sat on his throne, and took the ring.

It was also said: The body was Solomon himself, for he fell so severely ill that he became a body. The severely ill person is described by it, and it is said: "Like the cast-down body."

The description of Solomon's throne and his kingdom.

It is said on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: Sulayman would have six hundred thrones set out for him. Then the nobles of mankind would come and sit nearest to him, then the nobles of the jinn would come and sit next to mankind. Then he would call the birds, and they would shade them. Then he would call the wind, and it would carry them, and in a single morning it would travel the distance of a month.

Wahb, Ka'b and others said: When Sulayman, peace be upon him, became king after his father, he ordered that a throne be made for him to sit on for judging. He ordered that it be made in a wondrous and awe-inspiring form, so that whoever saw it, be he a wrongdoer or a false witness, would be deterred and awed. So he ordered that it be made of elephant tusks, inlaid with pearls, rubies and chrysolite, and that it be surrounded by golden palm trees. It was surrounded by four golden palm trees whose fronds were of red ruby and green emerald. On the top of two of the palm trees were golden peacocks, and on the top of two palm trees were golden eagles, facing one another. On either side of the throne they placed two golden lions, and on top of each of them was a pillar of green emerald.

They also wove over the palm trees vines of red gold, and made their clusters of red ruby, so that the canopy of the vines shaded the palm trees and the throne. When Sulayman, peace be upon him, wished to ascend it, he would place his feet on the lowest step, and the whole throne, with everything on it, would turn like a swiftly spinning millstone. The eagles and peacocks would spread their wings, the two lions would stretch out their forelegs, and they would strike the ground with their tails. This was done at every step that Sulayman climbed. When he reached the top, the two eagles that were on the palm trees would take Sulayman's crown and place it on his head. Then the throne would turn with everything on it, and the eagles, peacocks and two lions would turn with it, their heads inclined towards Sulayman, and they would sprinkle upon him musk and ambergris from their insides. Then a golden dove standing on a pillar of jewels above the throne would take up the Torah, and Sulayman, peace be upon him, would open it, read it to the people, and call them to decisive judgment.

They said: The leaders of the Children of Israel would sit on golden chairs inlaid with jewels, one thousand chairs to his right, and the leaders of the jinn would sit on silver chairs to his left, one thousand chairs. Then the birds would surround them and shade them, and the people would come forward for judgment. When the witnesses came forward to give their testimony, the throne would turn with everything on it and around him like a swiftly spinning millstone; the two lions would stretch out their forelegs and strike the ground with their tails, and the eagles and peacocks would spread their wings. The witnesses would be terrified, and they would testify only to the truth.

It was also said that what turned that throne was a golden serpent, upon which the throne rested, and it was greater than what Sakhr al-Jinni had made for him. When the eagles, lions and peacocks that were at the bottom of the throne sensed its turning, they would move up with it to the top. When they stopped, they would all stop at Sulayman's head while he was seated, and then they would all sprinkle upon his head what was in their insides of musk and ambergris.

When Sulayman died, Bakht Nasr sent someone who took the throne and carried it to Antioch. He wanted to ascend it, but he did not know how to climb it. When he placed his foot on it, the lion struck his leg and broke it, for Sulayman used to place both of his feet together when he climbed. Bakht Nasr died, and the throne was carried to Jerusalem. No king was ever able to sit on it. But no one knows the final outcome of its matter, and perhaps it was raised up (to heaven).

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Then he turned penitently﴾, meaning he returned to God and repented. This has already been discussed.

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿He said: "My Lord, forgive me"﴾, meaning forgive me my sin, "and grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me." It is asked: How could Sulayman seek worldly things when God has condemned them, hates them, and considers them insignificant? The answer is that the scholars interpret this as referring to the performance of God's rights, the governance of His kingdom, the ordering of the ranks of His creatures, the establishment of His limits, the preservation of His laws, the magnifying of His rituals, the manifestation of His worship, the necessity of obeying Him, and the ordering of the law of judgment that is enforced upon them by Him, and the fulfilment of the promise that He knows what none of His creatures knows, as He declared to His angels when He said: ﴿Indeed, I know what you do not know﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30]. Far be it from Sulayman, peace be upon him, that his request was a pursuit of the worldly life itself, for he and the prophets are the most detached of God's creatures from it. He only asked for its kingdom for God's sake, just as Nuh asked for its destruction and annihilation for God's sake. Both were praiseworthy and their requests were granted: Nuh's was answered and those upon the earth were destroyed, and Sulayman was given the kingdom. It has also been said that this was by a command from God, the Mighty and Majestic, in the manner that God knew only He could control, and no other of His servants could. Or he wished to say "a great kingdom," and then said: "that will not befit anyone after me." But this is questionable, and the first (view) is more correct.

Then He said to him: ﴿"This is Our gift, so give or withhold without account"﴾. Al-Hasan said: No one has been given a blessing by God except that he is held accountable for it, except Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon him, for He says: "This is Our gift" and so on. I say: This refutes what is reported in a khabar: "The last of the prophets to enter Paradise will be Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon him, because of his kingdom in this world." In some reports: "He will enter Paradise forty autumns after the prophets." This was mentioned by the author of al-Qut, and it is a hadith with no basis, because if His giving is without accountability, since it comes by way of grace, how could he be the last of the prophets to enter Paradise, when He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And indeed he has with Us a station of nearness and a good final return﴾? In the Sahih: "Every prophet has an answered supplication, and each prophet hastened his supplication," and the hadith continues. This has already been mentioned. So He made for him, before the request, a fulfilled need, and therefore there was no accountability for him. The meaning of his saying: "that will not befit anyone after me" is that no one should ask for it. It is as if he asked that no one else be allowed to ask after him, so that no one's hope would be attached to him, but he did not ask that the answer be withheld. It has also been said: His request for a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him was so that his place and honour with God would be manifest in the creation of the heavens and the earth. The prophets, peace be upon them, have a rivalry regarding their rank with Him, so each one loves to have a distinction by which his station with Him may be inferred. For this reason, when the Prophet (ﷺ) seized the 'ifrit who wanted to cut off his prayer, and God enabled him to overpower it, he wanted to tie it up, but then he remembered the words of his brother Sulayman: "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me," and so he sent it away humiliated. If anyone were given the like of it after him, the distinction would be gone, so he disliked that anyone should compete with him in that distinction, after he knew that it was a thing specific to him, the subjugation of the devils, and that he had been granted that no one would have it after him. And God knows best.

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running gently by his command wherever he wished﴾, meaning gentle despite its strength and power, so that it would not harm anyone, and it would carry him with his army, his troops and his procession. It is reported that his procession was a farsakh by a farsakh, a hundred levels one above another, each level a category of people, and he was at the highest level with his concubines, his attendants and his servants, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him.

Abu Nu'aym al-Hafiz mentioned: He narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Ja'far, who said: He narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, who said: He narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ayyub, who said: He narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash, from Idris ibn Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: My father narrated to me, saying: Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon him, had a thousand houses, the upper parts of which were of glass and the lower parts of iron. One day he rode the wind and passed by a ploughman, who looked at him and said: "The family of Dawud has been given a great kingdom!" The wind carried his words and cast them into Sulayman's ear. He said: So he descended until he came to the ploughman and said: "I heard your words, and I only came to you so that you would not wish for what you cannot have. A single glorification that God accepts from you is better than what the family of Dawud has been given." The ploughman said: "May God remove your worry as you have removed mine."

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿wherever he wished﴾, meaning wherever he intended. Mujahid said this. The Arabs say: "He hit the right thing and missed the answer" (aṣāba al-ṣawāb wa akhṭa'a al-jawāb), meaning he intended the right thing and missed the answer. Ibn al-A'rabi said this. A poet said:

*He hit upon the speech but could not...*
*and missed the answer at the joint.*

It is said that "aṣāba" means "intended" in the dialect of Himyar. Qatada said: it is in the language of Hajar. It is also said: "wherever he hit" means "whenever he aimed," derived from an arrow striking its intended target.

﴿And the devils, every builder and diver﴾, meaning We subjected to him the devils, and none had been subjected to anyone before him. "Every builder" is in apposition to "the devils," meaning every builder among them, so they would build for him whatever he wished. A poet said: [[This is al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani. Another version reads: "when the King said to him" and "then restrain them from the Fund." "Al-Fund" means error. "Khayyis" means subdue. "Al-Sifah" is the plural of "sifāḥa," which are thin, broad stones.]]

*Except Sulayman, when the God said to him:*
*"Stand among the wilderness and restrain them from error;*
*subdue the jinn, for I have permitted them*
*to build Tudmur with stone-slabs and pillars."*

"And diver" means in the sea, to bring up pearls for him. Sulayman was the first to have pearls extracted for him from the sea.

﴿And others bound together in shackles﴾, meaning We subjected to him the rebellious devils until he bound them in chains and iron fetters. Qatada said this. Al-Suddi said: "chains." Ibn 'Abbas said: "bonds." From this is the poet's saying [[This is 'Amr ibn Kulthum, and the verse is from his Mu'allaqa.]]:

*They returned with plunder and captives,*
*and we returned with kings in chains.*

Yahya ibn Sallam said: He would do this only to their disbelievers. When they believed, he would release them and not subject them.

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿"This is Our gift"﴾. The reference of "this" is to the kingdom: this kingdom is Our gift, so give to whomever you wish or withhold from whomever you wish, and there is no accountability for you. This is related from al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and others. Al-Hasan said: God has not bestowed a blessing on anyone except that he is held accountable for it, except Sulayman, peace be upon him, for God, the Exalted, says: "This is Our gift, so give or withhold without account." Qatada said: The reference in His saying "This is Our gift" is to what He gave him of power over intercourse. He had three hundred wives and seven hundred concubines, and in his loins was the semen of a hundred men. Ikrimah narrated this from Ibn 'Abbas [[Abu Hayyan said in his tafsir: "Perhaps this is not authentic from Ibn 'Abbas, because no mention of women has occurred here, nor of what he was given of power in that regard."]]. Its meaning is in al-Bukhari. And on this basis…

"Fa-mnun" (﻿فَامْنُنْ) is from al-mann (المَنّ), meaning the act of bestowing. It is said: amná yumnī and mana yamnī are two dialects; when you command one who uses amná, you say amni. It is also said: from mana yamnī fī al-amr, the command is imni; when you bring the nūn of the verb, the light nūn, you say "imnun." Whoever takes it to mean al-minna (favour) says: "manna ʿalayh" (he bestowed a favour upon him). When he puts it in the form of a command, he makes the two nūns manifest, because it is doubled, so he says "amnun" (﻿امْنُنْ).

It is related in the report that He subjected the devils to him, so whoever he wished he would bestow favour upon by freeing and releasing, and whoever he wished he would hold back. This is the view of Qatadah and al-Suddi. And according to what ʿIkrimah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: "Have intercourse with whichever of your wives you wish, and leave off intercourse with whichever of them you wish, with no reckoning against you."

"And indeed for him with Us is nearness and a good return" (﻿وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنا لَزُلْفى وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ): that is, if We bestow Our favour upon him in this world, then for him with Us in the Hereafter there is nearness (qurbah) and a good place of return (husn marji').

The commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 38, verses 34–40 (part 1 of 3):

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We certainly tried Solomon﴾. It was said: Solomon was tested after he had ruled for twenty years, and he ruled for twenty years after the trial. This was mentioned by al-Zamakhshari. "Fatannā" (we tried) means "ibtalaynā" (We tested) and "ʿāqabnā" (We punished). The cause of this is what Saʿid ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Two groups came to Solomon, peace be upon him, for judgment. One of them was from the people of Jarada, the wife of Solomon, whom he loved. He wished that the judgment would go in their favour. Then he judged between them with the truth, and what befell him was a punishment for that inclination.

Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib said: Solomon, peace be upon him, secluded himself from the people for three days, not judging between anyone and not granting justice to the wronged against the wrongdoer. So Allah the Exalted revealed to him: "I did not appoint you as a successor so that you would seclude yourself from My servants, but so that you would judge between them and grant justice to their wronged ones."

Shahr ibn Hawshab and Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Solomon, peace be upon him, captured the daughter of a king who had fought against him by sea, on an island among the islands of the sea called Sidon. Love for her was cast upon him, while she turned away from him. She would not look at him except sidelong, and would not speak to him except curtly. Her tears would not dry from grief for her father, and she was at the peak of beauty. Then she asked him to make for her a statue in the likeness of her father so that she could look at it. He ordered it made for her, and she revered it and prostrated to it, and her maidservants prostrated with her. It became an idol worshipped in his house while he did not know. Forty nights passed, and the news spread among the Children of Israel. Solomon learned of it, broke it, burned it, and then scattered it into the sea.

It was also said: When Solomon took the daughter of the king of Sidon, whose name was Jarada, according to what al-Zamakhshari mentioned, he admired her. He invited her to Islam, but she refused. He threatened her, and she said: "Kill me, but I will not become a Muslim." So he married her while she was a polytheist, and she used to worship an idol of hers made of ruby for forty days secretly from Solomon, until she became a Muslim. Solomon was punished by the loss of his kingdom for forty days.

Kaʿb al-Ahbar said: When he wronged the horses by killing them, his kingdom was taken from him.

al-Hasan said: He approached some of his wives during menstruation or something else.

It was also said: He was commanded not to marry any woman except from the Children of Israel, but he married a woman from outside them, and he was punished for that. And Allah knows best.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body﴾. It was said: It was a devil, according to the statement of most of the people of tafsir (exegesis). Allah cast upon it the likeness of Solomon, peace be upon him. His name was Sakhr ibn ʿUmayr, the Master of the Sea, and he is the one who guided Solomon to the diamond when Solomon ordered the building of Bayt al-Maqdis (the Holy House in Jerusalem). The stones would produce a sound when they were cut with iron, so they took diamonds and began to cut the stones, the gems, and other things with them, and they made no sound.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: He was a rebellious jinn whom all the devils could not overpower. He kept scheming until he obtained the ring of Solomon son of Dawud. Solomon would not enter the privy with his ring. So Sakhr came in the form of Solomon and took the ring from one of Solomon's women, a mother of a child of his called al-Amina, as Shahr and Wahb said. Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Jubayr said: Her name was Jarada. So he stood for forty days in Solomon's kingdom while Solomon was fleeing, until Allah restored the ring and the kingdom to him.

Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib said: Solomon had placed his ring under his bed, and the devil took it from under him.

Mujahid said: The devil took it from Solomon's hand, because Solomon asked the devil, whose name was Asif: "How do you lead people astray?" The devil said to him: "Give me your ring and I will tell you." So he gave him his ring. When the devil took the ring, he sat on Solomon's throne, taking his form, entering upon his wives, judging by other than the truth, and commanding other than what is right. [[These statements are certainly not authentic, because they contradict infallibility (ʿiṣmah), which is among the most distinctive attributes of the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them. Even if any of them were authentic, revelation would become subject to doubt and suspicion. Abu Hayyan said in his tafsir: "The exegetes have transmitted in this trial and the casting of the body statements that require the prophets to be absolved of them. They can be found in their books, and it is not permissible to transmit them. They are either fabrications of the Jews or the heretics. Allah did not specify what the trial was, nor the body that He cast upon Solomon's throne." He continued: "Someone whom the exegetes attribute to the one who is to be followed (i.e., Solomon) would not have said what is too grave to utter, and some of what they mentioned is impossible by reason, such as the devil taking the form of a prophet so that his affair becomes confused for the people, and they believe that the one they see is the prophet. Were this possible, one could not trust the sending of any prophet. This is merely a saying borrowed from the Sophists, the heretics. We ask Allah for the soundness of our minds and intellects from it." al-Alusi said: "Among the worst things in it is the claim that the devil gained power over the wives of his prophet to the point that he had intercourse with them while they were menstruating. Allahu Akbar!! This is a great slander and a grave matter." The author will also later weaken this statement.]]. There was a disagreement about his having intercourse with Solomon's wives. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas and Wahb ibn Munabbih that he used to approach them during their menstruation. Mujahid said: He was prevented from approaching them, and Solomon's kingdom was taken from him, so he fled to the seashore, begging from people and carrying the fish of the fishermen for a wage. Whenever he told people that he was Solomon, they called him a liar.

Qatada said: After the Children of Israel had disapproved of the judgment of the devil, Solomon took back his fish from a fisherman. It was said: He asked it as food. Ibn ʿAbbas said: He took it as a fee for carrying a fish. It was also said: Solomon caught it, and when he split its belly he found his ring inside it. This was forty days after the loss of his kingdom, which corresponds to the number of days during which the idol was worshipped in his house. He found the ring in the belly of the fish because the devil who had taken it had thrown it into the sea.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: While Solomon was on the seashore playing with his ring, it fell from him into the sea, and his kingdom was in his ring.

Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The engraving on the ring of Solomon son of Dawud was: There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

Yahya ibn Abi ʿAmr al-Shaybani related that Solomon found his ring in ʿAsqalan, and walked from there to Bayt al-Maqdis, humbling himself before Allah the Exalted.

Ibn ʿAbbas and others said: Then, when Allah restored his kingdom to Solomon, he seized Sakhr, who had taken his ring. He carved out a rock for him, put him inside it, sealed him in with another rock, fastened it with iron and lead, sealed it with his ring, and threw it into the sea, saying: "This is your prison until the Day of Resurrection."

ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, said: When Solomon took the ring, the devils, the jinn, the humans, the birds, the beasts, and the wind came to him. The devil who had been left in charge of his household fled and came to an island in the sea. They sent devils to him, and they said: "We cannot overpower him, but he comes to a spring on the island one day every seven days, and we cannot overpower him until he becomes intoxicated!" He said: So Solomon drained its water and put wine into it. When the day of its coming came, he found the wine and said: "By Allah, you are a good drink, except that you make the forbearing one act foolishly, and you increase the ignorant one in ignorance." Then he became extremely thirsty, and came to it again and said the same thing, and drank it. It overcame his mind, and they showed him the ring, and he said: "Hearing and obedience." They brought him to Solomon, who bound him and sent him to a mountain. They mentioned that it was the Mountain of Smoke, and said: "The smoke you see is from his breath, and the water that comes out of the mountain is from his urine."

Mujahid said: The name of that devil is Asif. Al-Suddi said: His name is Haqbiq. And Allah knows best. This statement has been weakened on the ground that the devil cannot take the form of the prophets, and also that it is impossible for the people of Solomon's kingdom to be confused about the devil being Solomon, so that they would think they were with their prophet in the truth, while they were with the devil in falsehood.

It was also said: The body was a child born to Solomon. When he was born, the devils gathered, and some of them said to others: "If a son survives to him, we will not be released from the trial and servitude we are in. So come, let us kill his son or maim him." Solomon learned of this, so he ordered the wind to carry the child up to the clouds, and his son grew up in the clouds, fearing the harm of the devils. Allah punished him through his fear of the devils, so he was not aware until he had fallen dead upon his throne. Al-Shaʿbi said this in meaning. This is the body of which Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body﴾.

al-Naqqash and others related: Solomon had most of his maidservants intercourse in pursuit of a child, so he had a child born to him who was half a human. This was the body placed upon his throne, which the midwife brought and then placed there.

In the Sahih of al-Bukhari and Muslim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Solomon said: Tonight I will go in to ninety women, and each of them will bear a horseman who will fight in the cause of Allah." His companion said to him: "Say: If Allah wills." But he did not say: "If Allah wills." So he went in to all of them, and only one woman became pregnant, and she brought forth half a man. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if he had said: "If Allah wills," they would have fought in the cause of Allah as horsemen, all of them."

It was also said: The body was Asif ibn Barkhiya, the truthful one, the scribe of Solomon. This is because when Solomon was tried, the ring fell from his hand, and his kingdom was in it. He put it back on his hand, and it fell again, and he became certain of the trial. Asif said to him: "You are being tested, and that is why it does not remain on your hand. So flee to Allah the Exalted, repenting of this. I will take your place in your world until Allah accepts your repentance. You have fourteen days from the time you were tried." So Solomon fled in haste to his Lord, and Asif took the ring and placed it on his hand, and it remained there. He had knowledge of the Book. Asif stood in Solomon's kingdom and his household, walking in his way and acting by his deeds, until Solomon returned to his home, repentant to Allah the Exalted, and Allah restored his kingdom to him. Then Asif remained in his place, sat on his throne, and took the ring.

It was also said: The body was Solomon himself, for he fell so severely ill that he became a body. The severely ill person is described by it, and it is said: "Like the cast-down body."

The description of Solomon's throne and his kingdom.

It is said on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: Sulayman would have six hundred thrones set out for him. Then the nobles of mankind would come and sit nearest to him, then the nobles of the jinn would come and sit next to mankind. Then he would call the birds, and they would shade them. Then he would call the wind, and it would carry them, and in a single morning it would travel the distance of a month.

Wahb, Ka'b and others said: When Sulayman, peace be upon him, became king after his father, he ordered that a throne be made for him to sit on for judging. He ordered that it be made in a wondrous and awe-inspiring form, so that whoever saw it, be he a wrongdoer or a false witness, would be deterred and awed. So he ordered that it be made of elephant tusks, inlaid with pearls, rubies and chrysolite, and that it be surrounded by golden palm trees. It was surrounded by four golden palm trees whose fronds were of red ruby and green emerald. On the top of two of the palm trees were golden peacocks, and on the top of two palm trees were golden eagles, facing one another. On either side of the throne they placed two golden lions, and on top of each of them was a pillar of green emerald.

They also wove over the palm trees vines of red gold, and made their clusters of red ruby, so that the canopy of the vines shaded the palm trees and the throne. When Sulayman, peace be upon him, wished to ascend it, he would place his feet on the lowest step, and the whole throne, with everything on it, would turn like a swiftly spinning millstone. The eagles and peacocks would spread their wings, the two lions would stretch out their forelegs, and they would strike the ground with their tails. This was done at every step that Sulayman climbed. When he reached the top, the two eagles that were on the palm trees would take Sulayman's crown and place it on his head. Then the throne would turn with everything on it, and the eagles, peacocks and two lions would turn with it, their heads inclined towards Sulayman, and they would sprinkle upon him musk and ambergris from their insides.
